newsitem.title: GERMANY: Japan says no G7 disagreement on forex.
newsitem.headline: Japan says no G7 disagreement on forex.

text.p: A Japanese finance ministry official said on Friday it would be wrong to assume that Japan and other Group of Seven members are in disagreement on currencies.
On the eve of a meeting of G7 finance ministers and central bank heads, another official in the Japanese delegation said currency stability was needed to ensure sustainable world economic growth.
In this context, the second official added, Japan would say at the G7 meeting that an overly weak or strong yen is unfavourable.

Asked if Japan may be left alone at the G7 meeting in its desire to check a further dollar rise, the first official told reporters, "It would be wrong to hold the view that Japan and the rest of the G7 are opposing each other on currencies."

Referring to comments made on Friday by U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin that the dollar has been strong for some time, the first official said: "Rubin has recently changed his remarks on the dollar subtly."
Rubin's remarks appeared to signal a subtle shift in the Clinton administration's preference for a strong dollar.
Japan fears that an overly strong dollar could lead its trade surplus to start ballooning again, and trigger a slide in the Tokyo stock market.
The Japanese economy has been recovering steadily, led by private-sector demand, the second official said.
"As I usually say, for the sustainable growth of the global economy, currency stability is quite significant," the second official said.
"We plan to tell the G7 meeting that an overly weak or strong yen is unfavourable," he said.
